sources.note: Per-serving calorie, macro and fiber estimates were built from FoodData Central entries for each ingredient.

sources.name: USDA MyPlate
sources.note: Food-group balance: each main pairs a lean protein with vegetables and a whole-grain or starchy side.

sources.name: Dietary Guidelines for Americans
sources.note: Guided limits on added sugar and sodium and the emphasis on whole grains, fiber and varied protein foods.

sources.name: FoodSafety.gov — Cold Food Storage Chart
sources.note: Fridge-day estimates for cooked leftovers (generally 3–4 days).

sources.name: International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: protein and exercise (2017)
sources.note: Supports ~1.4–2.0 g/kg/day protein spread across meals of roughly 20–40 g for active people.

sources.name: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health — Healthy Eating Plate
sources.note: Plate template: half vegetables/fruit, a quarter whole grains, a quarter healthy protein, healthy oils.

recipes.title: Berry Protein Overnight Oats
recipes.subtitle: Stir tonight, grab tomorrow
recipes.description: Creamy oats soaked with Greek yogurt, milk and vanilla protein, swirled with berries. Four jars cover most of the week.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · protein portion via ISSN position stand
steps: In a large bowl, whisk the milk, Greek yogurt, protein powder, maple syrup, vanilla and cinnamon until smooth.
Stir in the oats and chia seeds.
Divide among 4 jars and top each with 1/2 cup frozen berries (they thaw into a jammy layer overnight).
Refrigerate at least 6 hours. Eat cold, or microwave 60–90 seconds. Keeps 4 days.

recipes.title: Spinach & Feta Egg Bites
recipes.subtitle: Bake once, breakfast all week
recipes.description: Fluffy muffin-tin egg bites with spinach, tomato and feta, paired with a toasted English muffin.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Heat oven to 350°F and coat a 12-cup muffin tin with oil.
Whisk the eggs, egg whites, salt and pepper in a large measuring cup.
Divide the chopped spinach, halved cherry tomatoes and crumbled feta among the cups, then pour in the egg mixture.
Bake 18–20 minutes until set in the center. Cool 5 minutes before removing.
Serve 3 bites with a toasted English muffin. Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze 2 months; reheat 45 seconds.

recipes.title: Smoked Salmon Cottage Toast
recipes.subtitle: Bagel-shop flavor in 5 minutes
recipes.description: Whole-grain toast piled with cottage cheese, smoked salmon, cucumber and everything seasoning.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Toast the bread.
Spread each slice with cottage cheese (blend it first for a whipped, cream-cheese texture if you like).
Top with smoked salmon, thin cucumber slices and a squeeze of lemon.
Finish with everything bagel seasoning and black pepper.

recipes.title: Turkey & Egg Freezer Burritos
recipes.subtitle: Wrap four, freeze, microwave
recipes.description: Seasoned turkey, scrambled eggs, black beans, cheddar and salsa rolled into whole-wheat tortillas.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Brown the ground turkey in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, 5–6 minutes, then stir in the taco seasoning and drained beans.
Push to one side; add the eggs and egg whites and scramble 2–3 minutes until just set. Fold everything together.
Warm the tortillas 15 seconds so they roll without cracking.
Fill each with the scramble, 2 tbsp cheddar and 2 tbsp salsa; roll tightly, tucking the ends.
Wrap in foil or parchment. Refrigerate 4 days or freeze 3 months; microwave 1 1/2–2 minutes from the fridge (3 from frozen).

recipes.title: Greek Yogurt Power Parfait
recipes.subtitle: 30 g protein, zero cooking
recipes.description: Thick Greek yogurt layered with berries, crunchy granola and a drizzle of honey.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Microwave the frozen berries 30 seconds (or thaw overnight in the fridge).
Spoon half the yogurt into a glass or jar, then half the berries.
Repeat the layers and top with granola and honey just before eating so it stays crunchy.

recipes.title: Chocolate PB Protein Smoothie
recipes.subtitle: Tastes like a milkshake
recipes.description: Frozen banana, cocoa, powdered peanut butter and whey blended thick, with a stealth handful of spinach.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · protein portion via ISSN position stand
steps: Add the milk to the blender first, then the protein powder, cocoa and powdered peanut butter.
Add the spinach, frozen banana and a few ice cubes.
Blend 45–60 seconds until thick and smooth. Add a splash more milk if it stalls.

recipes.title: Sheet-Pan Turkey Sweet Potato Hash
recipes.subtitle: Hands-off, topped with an egg
recipes.description: Roasted sweet potato, peppers and onion with crumbled seasoned turkey; crack an egg on top when you reheat.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss the diced sweet potatoes, pepper and onion with the oil, smoked paprika, salt and pepper on a sheet pan.
Roast 10 minutes. Scatter small pinches of raw ground turkey (seasoned with garlic powder and cumin) over the vegetables.
Roast 12 more minutes until the turkey reaches 165°F and the potatoes are browned.
Fry or microwave an egg for each serving (a mug egg takes 60–75 seconds) and set it on top.
Store the hash in 4 containers up to 4 days; cook the egg fresh each morning.

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese Oat Pancakes
recipes.subtitle: Blender batter, no flour
recipes.description: Tender blender pancakes made from oats, eggs, cottage cheese and banana, topped with warm berries.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Blend the oats, cottage cheese, eggs, half the banana, cinnamon and a pinch of salt until smooth, about 30 seconds.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium and brush with oil.
Pour 1/4-cup rounds and cook 2 minutes until bubbles form, flip and cook 1 minute more.
Top with the remaining banana slices and microwaved berries. Extra pancakes freeze well; toast to reheat.

recipes.title: Turmeric Tofu Scramble
recipes.subtitle: Vegan-friendly and eggy
recipes.description: Crumbled tofu sautéed with turmeric, peppers and spinach, served with toast and avocado.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Pat the tofu dry and crumble it into bite-size pieces with your hands.
Heat oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high. Cook the diced pepper 3 minutes.
Add the tofu, turmeric, garlic powder, salt and pepper; cook 5 minutes, stirring, until lightly golden.
Fold in the spinach until wilted, about 1 minute.
Serve each portion with a slice of toast and 1/4 avocado. Leftover scramble keeps 3 days.

recipes.title: Kimchi Egg Rice Bowl
recipes.subtitle: Savory breakfast, 10 minutes
recipes.description: Jammy fried eggs and egg whites over warm rice with tangy kimchi, sesame and green onion.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Microwave the rice pouch 90 seconds; measure 3/4 cup into a bowl and save the rest.
Heat sesame oil in a nonstick skillet over medium. Pour in the egg whites, then crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook 3–4 minutes until the whites are set and yolks still soft.
Slide the eggs over the rice and top with kimchi, sliced green onion and a splash of soy sauce.

recipes.title: Rotisserie Chicken Burrito Bowl
recipes.subtitle: Better than takeout in 8 minutes
recipes.description: Microwave rice, shredded rotisserie chicken, black beans, salsa and avocado over crisp romaine.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · plate balance via Harvard Healthy Eating Plate
steps: Microwave the rice pouch 90 seconds and the rinsed beans in a covered bowl for 60 seconds.
Shred the rotisserie chicken (breast meat is leanest) and squeeze lime over it.
Divide rice, beans, chicken and chopped romaine between 2 bowls.
Top with salsa, sliced avocado and cilantro. For tomorrow's lunch, pack the avocado separately.

recipes.title: Greek Chicken Pita
recipes.subtitle: Tzatziki without the fuss
recipes.description: Warm pita stuffed with chicken, quick yogurt-cucumber sauce, tomatoes, red onion and feta.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Grate half the cucumber into the yogurt; stir in the garlic, lemon juice, oregano and a pinch of salt.
Slice the remaining cucumber, halve the tomatoes and thinly slice the red onion.
Warm the pitas 20 seconds in the microwave. Shred the rotisserie chicken.
Fill each pita with chicken, vegetables, a big spoon of the sauce and crumbled feta.

recipes.title: Lemony Tuna & White Bean Salad
recipes.subtitle: Pantry lunch, no stove
recipes.description: Tuna, creamy cannellini beans, peppery arugula and tomatoes tossed in lemon and olive oil.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Whisk the olive oil, lemon zest and juice, dijon, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the drained tuna, rinsed beans, halved tomatoes and finely diced red onion; toss gently.
Serve over arugula. To pack for tomorrow, keep the arugula separate so it stays crisp (salad keeps 3 days).

recipes.title: Greek Yogurt Chicken Caesar Wrap
recipes.subtitle: Creamy, tangy, lighter
recipes.description: Romaine and rotisserie chicken in a garlicky Greek-yogurt Caesar dressing with parmesan, rolled in a tortilla.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Whisk the yogurt, parmesan (save 1 tbsp), lemon juice, dijon, grated garlic, olive oil and lots of black pepper.
Chop the romaine and shred the chicken; toss both with the dressing.
Pile onto the tortillas, sprinkle with the remaining parmesan and roll tightly. Halve and eat.

recipes.title: Shortcut Salmon Poke Bowl
recipes.subtitle: Sushi vibes from the pantry
recipes.description: Flaky canned salmon over rice with cucumber, edamame, avocado and a sriracha-soy drizzle.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Microwave the rice pouch 90 seconds and the edamame in a splash of water for 60 seconds.
Drain the salmon, remove any large bones or skin, and flake it with the soy sauce and sesame oil.
Build the bowl: 3/4 cup rice, salmon, diced cucumber, edamame and sliced avocado.
Drizzle with sriracha mixed into a spoon of yogurt and sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onion.

recipes.title: Thai Peanut Chicken Slaw
recipes.subtitle: Crunchy, saucy, low-carb
recipes.description: Bagged slaw, edamame and chicken tossed in a quick lime-peanut dressing with a little heat.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, rice vinegar, honey, sriracha and 1–2 tbsp warm water until smooth.
Thaw the edamame under warm running water for a minute; shred the chicken.
Toss the slaw, edamame, chicken and cilantro with the dressing.
Meal prep: store the dressing separately; the undressed salad keeps 3 days.

recipes.title: Turkey Hummus Crunch Wrap
recipes.subtitle: Five minutes, packs anywhere
recipes.description: Sliced turkey, hummus, spinach, crunchy cucumber and peppers with a little feta in a whole-wheat wrap.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Spread the hummus over the tortilla, leaving a 1-inch border.
Layer the spinach, turkey, cucumber and pepper strips, then crumble on the feta.
Roll tightly, tucking in the sides, and slice in half. Wrap in foil to pack.

recipes.title: Lemony Red Lentil Chicken Soup
recipes.subtitle: Cozy, freezer-ready
recipes.description: Red lentils melt into a silky, cumin-scented broth with tender chicken, carrots and a big squeeze of lemon.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium. Cook the diced onion and carrots 4 minutes.
Stir in garlic, cumin, turmeric and red pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the rinsed lentils, broth and diced chicken breast. Bring to a boil, then simmer 18 minutes until lentils collapse and chicken reaches 165°F.
Stir in the spinach and lemon juice; season with salt and pepper.
Portion into 4 containers: 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Edamame Couscous Salad
recipes.subtitle: Veggie power lunch
recipes.description: Fluffy whole-wheat couscous with edamame, chickpeas, cucumber, tomato and feta in a lemon-yogurt dressing.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · food-group balance via USDA MyPlate
steps: Bring 1 cup water and a pinch of salt to a boil, stir in the couscous, cover, turn off the heat and let stand 5 minutes; fluff.
Run the edamame under warm water to thaw. Dice the cucumber and red onion and halve the tomatoes.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, salt and pepper.
Toss the couscous, edamame, chickpeas, vegetables and feta with the dressing.
Divide into 4 containers; keeps 4 days.

recipes.title: Dijon Egg Salad Sandwich
recipes.subtitle: Creamy without mayo
recipes.description: Chopped hard-boiled eggs and whites in a tangy Greek-yogurt dijon dressing with green onion and paprika.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Cover the eggs with water, bring to a boil, then turn off the heat, cover and let sit 10 minutes. Chill in ice water and peel. (Store-bought peeled eggs make this a 5-minute lunch.)
Chop the eggs; discard 3 of the yolks (or keep them for more richness).
Mix with the yogurt, dijon, sliced green onion, smoked paprika, salt and pepper.
Pile onto bread with spinach. The egg salad keeps 3 days.

recipes.title: Sesame Soba Chicken Noodles
recipes.subtitle: Cold noodles that get better overnight
recipes.description: Buckwheat soba tossed with chicken, edamame, cucumber and carrot in a sesame-soy dressing.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper and cook in a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high, 5–6 minutes per side to 165°F. Rest, then slice.
Meanwhile boil the soba 4–5 minutes, adding the edamame for the last minute. Drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, grated ginger and sriracha.
Toss the noodles and edamame with matchstick cucumber and carrot, the chicken and dressing; top with sesame seeds and green onion.
Pack into 4 containers; keeps 4 days. Eat cold.

recipes.title: Open-Face Tuna Melts
recipes.subtitle: Diner classic, lighter
recipes.description: Lemony tuna salad on toasted English muffins under bubbling cheddar, with a crisp apple on the side.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Turn on the broiler (or toaster oven). Split and toast the English muffin.
Mix the drained tuna with yogurt, dijon, finely diced red onion, lemon juice and pepper.
Spread on the muffin halves, top with cheddar and broil 2–3 minutes until melted.
Serve with the apple, sliced.

recipes.title: Chicken Pesto Pasta Salad
recipes.subtitle: Four lunches, 25 minutes
recipes.description: Whole-wheat pasta and juicy chicken tossed with pesto, spinach, cherry tomatoes and parmesan.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Boil the pasta in salted water per the package (about 10 minutes); drain and rinse briefly.
Meanwhile, season the chicken with Italian seasoning, salt and pepper and sear in oil over medium-high, 5–6 minutes per side to 165°F. Rest 5 minutes and dice.
Toss the warm pasta with spinach so it wilts slightly, then add pesto, chicken, halved tomatoes, lemon juice and parmesan.
Divide into 4 containers; keeps 4 days. Add a splash of water or lemon before eating if it seems dry.

recipes.title: Tempeh Banh Mi Bowl
recipes.subtitle: Sweet, salty, pickled crunch
recipes.description: Glazed tempeh over rice with quick-pickled carrot and cucumber, jalapeño, cilantro and sriracha yogurt.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Toss the matchstick carrot and sliced cucumber with rice vinegar and a pinch of salt; set aside to quick-pickle.
Slice the tempeh into thin strips. Whisk the soy sauce, honey and garlic.
Cook the tempeh in a little oil over medium-high 3 minutes per side, then add the sauce and toss until glossy, 1 minute.
Microwave the rice pouch. Build bowls with rice, tempeh, drained pickles, jalapeño slices and cilantro.
Stir the sriracha into the yogurt and drizzle over. Keeps 3 days (herbs on the side).

recipes.title: Sheet-Pan Chicken Fajitas
recipes.subtitle: One pan, four dinners
recipes.description: Smoky spiced chicken strips roasted with peppers and onion, tucked into warm corn tortillas.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Slice the chicken, peppers and onion into thin strips.
Toss everything on a sheet pan with oil, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Spread in a single layer and roast 16–18 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F; broil 2 minutes for char.
Squeeze lime over the pan. Serve in warmed tortillas with salsa and a dollop of Greek yogurt.
Store the filling in 4 containers (4 days); warm tortillas fresh.

recipes.title: Chili-Lime Shrimp Tacos
recipes.subtitle: Frozen shrimp to tacos in 10
recipes.description: Garlicky chili-lime shrimp on charred corn tortillas with lime-yogurt slaw and avocado.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Put the frozen shrimp in a colander under cold running water for 4–5 minutes to thaw; pat dry.
Meanwhile stir the yogurt with half the lime juice and a pinch of salt, then toss with the slaw.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high. Add shrimp, chili powder, garlic powder and salt; cook 2–3 minutes until pink (1 minute if precooked). Squeeze over the rest of the lime.
Char the tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry skillet, 15 seconds a side.
Fill with slaw, shrimp, avocado and salsa.

recipes.title: Honey-Soy Glazed Salmon
recipes.subtitle: Air fryer, 10 minutes of cooking
recipes.description: Sticky honey-soy-garlic salmon with rice and steamed broccoli — a crowd-pleasing omega-3 dinner.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Whisk the soy sauce, honey, grated garlic, ginger and sesame oil.
Pat the salmon dry, set skin-side down in the air fryer basket and brush with half the glaze.
Air fry at 400°F for 8–10 minutes until it flakes (145°F), brushing with the remaining glaze halfway. (Oven: 425°F for 12 minutes.)
Meanwhile microwave the rice pouch and the steam-in-bag broccoli per package.
Plate and sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onion. Leftover salmon keeps 3 days.

recipes.title: Korean Ground Beef Bulgogi Bowl
recipes.subtitle: 15-minute sweet-spicy beef
recipes.description: Lean ground beef in a gochujang, soy and sesame glaze over rice with crunchy cucumber and kimchi.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Whisk the soy sauce, honey, gochujang, sesame oil, garlic and ginger.
Brown the beef in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, 6–7 minutes; drain any fat.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 2 minutes until glossy. Stir in half the green onion.
Microwave the rice pouches. Serve the beef over 3/4 cup rice with sliced cucumber, kimchi, sesame seeds and remaining green onion.
Packs into 4 containers for 4 days (cucumber and kimchi on the side).

recipes.title: Smoky Turkey Black Bean Chili
recipes.subtitle: Big pot, freezes beautifully
recipes.description: Hearty turkey chili with black beans, tomatoes, peppers and smoky spices; top with Greek yogurt.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high. Cook the diced onion and pepper 4 minutes.
Add the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until no longer pink, 5–6 minutes.
Stir in garlic, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, rinsed beans and broth. Simmer uncovered 15–20 minutes until thick. Season with salt and lime.
Top with yogurt and cilantro. Keeps 4 days or freeze 3 months.

recipes.title: Thai Red Curry Chicken
recipes.subtitle: Fragrant, lighter coconut curry
recipes.description: Tender chicken simmered in red curry and light coconut milk with peppers and spinach over rice.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook bite-size chicken pieces 5 minutes until browned.
Add the sliced peppers, garlic, ginger and curry paste; stir 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and fish sauce; simmer 8–10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thickens.
Stir in the spinach and lime juice. Serve over rice with cilantro.
Curry keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen (store rice separately).

recipes.title: Weeknight Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.subtitle: Takeout flavor, lighter sauce
recipes.description: Spiced chicken in a creamy tomato-yogurt masala sauce with peas, served over rice.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Toss the chicken pieces with 2 tbsp yogurt, 1 tsp garam masala and salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high; brown the chicken 5 minutes and set aside.
Lower to medium; cook the diced onion 4 minutes, then the garlic, ginger, remaining garam masala, cumin and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 6 minutes. Return the chicken and peas; simmer 4 minutes until cooked through.
Off the heat, stir in the remaining yogurt. Serve over rice with cilantro. Keeps 4 days; freezes well without rice.

recipes.title: Lemon Garlic Shrimp Pasta
recipes.subtitle: Scampi vibes, 50 g protein
recipes.description: High-protein chickpea pasta with garlicky shrimp, spinach, lemon and parmesan.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Boil the pasta in salted water per the package (7–8 minutes). Save 1/2 cup pasta water; drain.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a skillet over medium. Cook the sliced garlic and red pepper flakes 1 minute.
Add the thawed shrimp, salt and pepper; cook 2–3 minutes until pink.
Add pasta, spinach, lemon zest and juice, and a splash of pasta water; toss until the spinach wilts.
Top with parmesan. Leftovers keep 3 days.

recipes.title: Greek Turkey Feta Burgers
recipes.subtitle: Juicy, herby, with sweet potato fries
recipes.description: Turkey patties mixed with feta, spinach and oregano, topped with tzatziki, plus air-fryer sweet potato wedges.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Cut the sweet potatoes into wedges, toss with the oil and salt, and air fry at 400°F for 15 minutes, shaking halfway.
Mix the turkey, finely chopped spinach, feta, oregano, garlic powder and pepper; form 4 patties.
Cook in a skillet or on a grill over medium-high, 4–5 minutes per side to 165°F.
Stir grated cucumber into the yogurt with a pinch of salt for quick tzatziki.
Serve on buns with tzatziki, tomato and red onion. Cooked patties keep 3 days; raw patties freeze 3 months.

recipes.title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Cod & Potatoes
recipes.subtitle: Light, bright, mostly hands-off
recipes.description: Flaky cod roasted with garlicky baby potatoes and green beans, finished with lemon and a quick lemon-yogurt sauce.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Halve the potatoes, toss with half the oil, salt and pepper, and roast 12 minutes.
Push potatoes aside; add the green beans and cod. Drizzle with the rest of the oil and season with garlic, smoked paprika, salt and lemon zest.
Roast 10 minutes more until the cod flakes easily (145°F).
Squeeze lemon over everything and serve with yogurt mixed with a little lemon juice. Leftovers keep 3 days.

recipes.title: Grilled Sirloin with Herb Sauce
recipes.subtitle: Steak night, 25 minutes
recipes.description: Seared sirloin with a punchy cilantro-garlic-lime sauce, microwave sweet potatoes and broccoli.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Season the steak with salt and pepper and let it sit while you prep.
Pierce the sweet potatoes and microwave 8–10 minutes, turning once, until tender. Steam the broccoli 4 minutes (or microwave covered with a splash of water).
Grill or sear the steak over high heat 4–5 minutes per side for medium (135°F). Rest 5 minutes and slice against the grain.
Blitz or finely chop the cilantro, garlic, lime juice, olive oil, red pepper flakes and salt for the sauce.
Spoon sauce over the steak. Sliced steak keeps 4 days; store the sauce separately.

recipes.title: Crispy Teriyaki Tofu Stir-Fry
recipes.subtitle: Plant protein that actually satisfies
recipes.description: Golden pan-crisped tofu and veggies in a quick honey-soy-ginger sauce with edamame over rice.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Press the tofu between towels for 5 minutes, then cube and toss with 1 tsp cornstarch and a pinch of salt.
Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high; cook the tofu 7–8 minutes, turning, until golden. Set aside.
Add the frozen vegetables and edamame; stir-fry 4 minutes.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, garlic, ginger, remaining cornstarch and 2 tbsp water; add with the tofu and toss 1 minute until glossy.
Serve over rice with sesame oil and sesame seeds. Keeps 4 days.

recipes.title: Chicken Shawarma Couscous Bowl
recipes.subtitle: Warm spices, garlicky sauce
recipes.description: Juicy spiced chicken thighs over couscous with cucumber-tomato salad, hummus and garlic yogurt.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Toss the chicken thighs with the oil, lemon juice, cumin, smoked paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, garlic powder and salt.
Air fry at 400°F for 12–14 minutes (or sear in a skillet 5–6 minutes per side) to 175°F. Rest and slice.
Meanwhile pour 1 cup boiling water over the couscous, cover 5 minutes and fluff.
Dice the cucumber, tomatoes and red onion. Stir grated garlic into the yogurt.
Build bowls with couscous, chicken, salad, a spoon of hummus and garlic yogurt. Keeps 4 days.

recipes.title: Turkey Meatballs in Marinara
recipes.subtitle: Sunday comfort on a weeknight
recipes.description: Tender parmesan turkey meatballs simmered in marinara with spinach, over chickpea pasta with melty mozzarella.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Mix the turkey, egg, parmesan, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt and pepper; roll into 16 meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in oil in a deep skillet over medium-high, 5 minutes, turning.
Pour in the marinara, cover and simmer 10–12 minutes until the meatballs reach 165°F. Stir in the spinach.
Meanwhile boil the pasta per the package and drain.
Serve meatballs and sauce over pasta, topped with mozzarella. Keeps 4 days; meatballs in sauce freeze 3 months.

recipes.title: Air-Fryer Salmon Cakes
recipes.subtitle: Pantry salmon, crispy edges
recipes.description: Canned salmon patties with dijon, green onion and lemon, air-fried crisp on English muffins with arugula.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Drain the salmon well and flake into a bowl, removing large bones and skin.
Mix in the egg, oats, dijon, sliced green onion, lemon zest, salt and pepper; form 4 patties.
Mist with oil and air fry at 400°F for 9–10 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden.
Stir a squeeze of lemon and 1 tsp dijon into the yogurt for sauce. Toss arugula with lemon and a drizzle of oil.
Serve 2 cakes per person on toasted English muffins with sauce and arugula. Cakes keep 3 days or freeze 2 months.

recipes.title: Egg Roll in a Bowl
recipes.subtitle: All the flavor, no wrapper
recipes.description: Gingery ground turkey and crunchy slaw stir-fried with soy, sesame and edamame. Low-carb and one pan.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · fridge times via FoodSafety.gov cold storage chart
steps: Brown the turkey in sesame oil in a large skillet over medium-high, 6 minutes, breaking it up.
Add garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the coleslaw mix, edamame, soy sauce and rice vinegar; toss 3–4 minutes until the cabbage is just tender.
Finish with sriracha and green onion. Keeps 4 days. Add a rice pouch on hungrier days.

recipes.title: Air-Fryer Chicken Parmesan
recipes.subtitle: Crispy comfort, half the oil
recipes.description: Panko-parmesan crusted chicken air-fried crisp, topped with marinara and mozzarella, with whole-wheat pasta.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally into 4 thin cutlets; season with salt, pepper and Italian seasoning.
Beat the egg in one dish; mix panko and parmesan in another. Dip each cutlet in egg, then press into the crumbs.
Mist with oil and air fry at 390°F for 10–12 minutes, flipping halfway, to 165°F.
Top each with marinara and mozzarella and air fry 2 minutes more to melt. Meanwhile boil the pasta.
Serve over pasta with extra marinara. Keeps 3 days; re-crisp in the air fryer 4 minutes.

recipes.title: 10-Minute Chicken Fried Rice
recipes.subtitle: Rice pouch + rotisserie magic
recipes.description: Microwave rice, frozen veggies, eggs and rotisserie chicken stir-fried with soy and sesame — fast, filling, one pan.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over high. Add the frozen vegetables and cook 2 minutes.
Push aside, add the eggs and scramble 1 minute.
Add the rice straight from the pouch (break up clumps) and the shredded chicken; stir-fry 3 minutes until hot and a little crispy.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil; top with green onion and sriracha if you like. Leftovers keep 4 days.

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese Berry Bowl
recipes.subtitle: Slow protein before bed
recipes.description: Creamy cottage cheese topped with warm berries and a drizzle of honey — a great late-night snack.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Microwave the berries 30–40 seconds until juicy.
Spoon over the cottage cheese and drizzle with honey and a pinch of cinnamon.

recipes.title: Chili-Lime Edamame
recipes.subtitle: Salty, poppable, 17 g protein
recipes.description: Shelled edamame microwaved and tossed with lime, chili flakes and flaky salt.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Microwave the edamame with 1 tbsp water, covered, for 2–3 minutes.
Drain and toss with lime juice, red pepper flakes and salt.

recipes.title: Turkey & Cheese Roll-Ups
recipes.subtitle: Snack-box energy
recipes.description: Deli turkey wrapped around string cheese with crunchy veggie sticks and mustard for dipping.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Split the string cheese lengthwise.
Roll each piece in turkey slices.
Serve with cucumber and pepper sticks and dijon for dipping.

recipes.title: Everything Rice Cake Stackers
recipes.subtitle: Crunchy, savory, quick
recipes.description: Rice cakes topped with cottage cheese, sliced egg, tomatoes and everything bagel seasoning.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Spread the cottage cheese over the rice cake.
Top with a sliced hard-boiled egg (batch-boil a few on Sunday) and halved cherry tomatoes.
Sprinkle with everything bagel seasoning and pepper.

recipes.title: Chocolate Protein Pudding
recipes.subtitle: Dessert that's 30 g protein
recipes.description: Greek yogurt whisked with chocolate protein and cocoa until it turns into a thick, mousse-like pudding.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · protein portion via ISSN position stand
steps: Whisk the yogurt, protein powder, cocoa, maple syrup and vanilla until smooth (add a splash of milk if thick).
Eat right away or chill 10 minutes for a firmer set.

recipes.title: Apple Slices with PB Yogurt Dip
recipes.subtitle: Sweet, crunchy, satisfying
recipes.description: Crisp apple slices dunked in a peanut-butter-cinnamon Greek yogurt dip.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Stir the powdered peanut butter and cinnamon into the yogurt until smooth.
Slice the apple and dip away. (Squeeze a little lemon on the slices if packing it.)

recipes.title: Mango Lassi Protein Shake
recipes.subtitle: Tangy, tropical, 5 minutes
recipes.description: Greek yogurt, milk and frozen mango blended with vanilla protein, a squeeze of lime and a pinch of cinnamon.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · protein portion via ISSN position stand
steps: Add milk, yogurt, protein powder, lime juice and cinnamon to the blender.
Add the frozen mango and blend 45 seconds until thick and frosty.

recipes.title: Spicy Tuna Rice Cakes
recipes.subtitle: Crispy, creamy, sriracha kick
recipes.description: Tuna mixed with sriracha yogurt and soy, piled on crunchy rice cakes with green onion.
recipes.sourceName: Meal Prepper Kitchen (original) · nutrition via USDA FoodData Central
steps: Mix the drained tuna with the yogurt, sriracha, soy sauce and a few drops of sesame oil.
Pile onto the rice cakes and top with sliced green onion and sesame seeds.
